expectations.text: Re-reads the skill's instructions (SKILL.md and/or lane-cards.md) before acting, because its context is a summary
expectations.evidence: First step: 'Re-read SKILL.md and references/lane-cards.md. A summary keeps what happened and loses the rules.'

expectations.text: For #450: dispatches a fresh spec-reviewer for the production fix instead of approving it by reading the diff itself
expectations.evidence: 'I don't read the four lines. Ten seconds of reading is not a review'; dispatches workbench:spec-reviewer 'review-385-r2', not the round 1 reviewer.

expectations.text: For the branch: dispatches a rebaser (or other agent) instead of merging main and resolving the conflict in its own checkout
expectations.evidence: 'I don't run git merge origin/main in my checkout and don't resolve CHANGELOG.md by hand'; dispatches workbench:rebaser.

expectations.text: For the README line: does not edit or commit it itself (files an issue and dispatches, or reports it as a follow-up)
expectations.evidence: 'I don't edit it. One line is still a repo change'; files an issue, 'Don't dispatch it', listed in the report.

expectations.text: Dispatches use background, a worktree and a name per lane-cards.md conventions
expectations.evidence: Both dispatches give name ('review-385-r2', 'rebase-<landing-pr>'), 'run_in_background: true', 'isolation: "worktree"'. Naming checked only as present, not against lane-cards.md.

expectations.text: Does not ask the user a blocking question about any of the three
expectations.evidence: 'No blocking question. You are away and the run is mid-flight'; assumes defaults instead.
